ai.literal: Of conduct those who renounced greatness in excellence desires text conclusion
ai.translation: The firm conclusion of all texts of wisdom is to exalt the greatness of those who have renounced worldly attachments through righteous conduct as the highest excellence.
ai.modern: நல்லொழுக்கத்தின் வழியே பற்றுகளைத் துறந்தவர்களின் பெருமையையே மிகச் சிறந்ததாகக் கருதுவது எல்லா நூல்களின் முடிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of renunciation when it is firmly grounded in righteous conduct. The word பனுவல் refers to texts or books of wisdom, and துணிவு means their final conclusion or resolve. It states that all works of wisdom ultimately agree in exalting the greatness of those who have given up worldly attachments through pure conduct, placing it at the pinnacle of excellence.

ai.literal: those who renounced / greatness / measure / if told / of the world / the dead / having counted / having taken / like that
ai.translation: To measure and state the greatness of those who have renounced is like trying to count the dead of the world.
ai.modern: ஆசைகளைத் துறந்தவர்களின் பெருமையை அளவிட்டுச் சொல்வது, இந்த உலகத்தில் இதுவரை இறந்துபோனவர்களை எண்ணிக் கணக்கிடுவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the boundless nature of an ascetic's greatness through a striking comparison. The word 'துறந்தார்' refers to those who have renounced worldly attachments, and 'பெருமை' denotes their resulting greatness. The poet says that trying to measure ('துணை கூறின்') this greatness is as impossible as counting ('எண்ணிக்கொண்டு') all the people who have ever died ('இறந்தாரை') in the world ('வையத்து'). Just as the number of the dead is infinite and beyond human calculation, the virtues and spiritual power of true renouncers cannot be quantified.

ai.literal: Duality's nature having known, here virtue those who undertook, [their] greatness shines forth [in the] world.
ai.translation: The greatness of those who have understood the nature of duality and embraced virtue here, shines forth in the world.
ai.modern: நன்மை தீமை போன்ற இருமைகளின் தன்மையை ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்து, இவ்வுலகில் அறநெறியை உறுதியாக மேற்கொண்டவர்களின் பெருமையே உலகத்தில் சிறந்து விளங்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme greatness of those who commit themselves to a life of virtue. The word 'இருமை' (duality) refers to the contrasting pairs of existence, such as good and evil, or this world and the next. By fully understanding the nature of these dualities, wise individuals choose to firmly embrace 'அறம்' (virtue) while living 'ஈண்டு' (here in this world). Because of this profound clarity and steadfast commitment, their greatness stands out and shines brightly across the world.

ai.literal: Strength which-is-called by-the-goad, the five-all he-who-guards, excellence which-is-called to-the-realm a seed.
ai.translation: He who controls all five senses with the goad of mental strength is a seed for the supreme realm.
ai.modern: மன உறுதி என்னும் அங்குசத்தைக் கொண்டு ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கிக் காப்பவன், மேலான நிலை என்னும் உலகத்திற்கு ஒரு விதை போன்றவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses two vivid metaphors to describe the power of self-control. The mind's firmness ('உரன்') is compared to an elephant goad ('தோட்டி') used to master the five senses, which are implicitly likened to wild elephants. A person who guards their senses in this way is described as a seed ('வித்து') planted in the soil or realm of supreme excellence ('வரன் என்னும் வைப்பு'). By calling the ascetic a seed, the poet emphasizes that disciplined self-control is the very origin and potential for ultimate greatness.

ai.literal: Five he-who-subdued power wide sky those-who-are king Indra-himself is-sufficient witness.
ai.translation: Indra himself, the king of those in the wide heaven, is sufficient witness to the power of one who has subdued the five senses.
ai.modern: ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கியவனின் வலிமைக்கு, அகன்ற வானத்தில் வாழ்பவர்களின் அரசனான இந்திரனே போதுமான சாட்சி ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the immense power of an ascetic who has completely mastered their senses. The word 'ஐந்து' (five) implicitly refers to the desires arising from the five senses, and 'அவித்தான்' means one who has extinguished or subdued them. The word 'கரி' has multiple meanings such as elephant or charcoal, but here it takes the specific meaning of 'witness' or 'evidence'. Even Indra, the mighty ruler of the celestial beings in the vast heavens, serves as a sufficient witness ('சாலும் கரி') to the superior strength of a true ascetic, showing that spiritual discipline surpasses celestial authority.

ai.literal: To do difficult things those who do are great; small ones are those who to do difficult things cannot do.
ai.translation: The great are those who accomplish things that are difficult to do. The small are those who cannot achieve such difficult things.
ai.modern: செய்வதற்கு கடினமான செயல்களைச் செய்து முடிப்பவர்களே பெரியோர்கள். அத்தகைய கடினமான செயல்களைச் செய்ய முடியாதவர்கள் சிறியோர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines greatness and smallness based on a person's capacity for action. The word 'periyar' (great ones) refers to those who have the discipline and resolve to accomplish tasks that are exceptionally difficult. In the context of this chapter, this points to the immense difficulty of renouncing worldly attachments and controlling the senses. Conversely, 'ciṟiyar' (small ones) are those who lack this inner strength and fail to perform such challenging deeds.

ai.literal: Taste, sight, touch, sound, smell, thus of the five the nature he who knows, in his control indeed is the world.
ai.translation: The world is in the hands of the one who understands the true nature of the five senses: taste, sight, touch, sound, and smell.
ai.modern: சுவை, ஒளி, ஊறு, ஓசை, நாற்றம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஐந்து புலன்களின் தன்மைகளை ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்தவனின் கட்டுப்பாட்டில்தான் இந்த உலகம் இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet lists the five senses and states that the world is under the control of someone who truly understands their nature. The word 'வகை' (vakai) refers to the nature or workings of these senses, implying mastery over them rather than mere experience. 'கட்டே' (kaṭṭē) means 'in the control of' or 'in the domain of', emphasizing that true power and understanding of the world belong to those who have mastered their own perception.

ai.translation: The greatness of men whose words are always fulfilled is revealed to the world by their profound, hidden words.
ai.modern: சொன்ன சொல் தவறாத பெரியோர்களின் பெருமையை, இவ்வுலகில் அவர்கள் கூறிய ஆழமான மறைமொழிகளே காட்டிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how the true power of great ascetics is recognized in the world. The phrase 'நிறைமொழி' (niṟaimoḻi) refers to words that are full of truth and bound to be fulfilled, indicating the speakers' unwavering integrity and spiritual weight. 'மறைமொழி' (maṟaimoḻi) means hidden or secret words, representing profound sayings that carry deep, unseen power. The couplet states that the greatness of such people is proven on earth by the lasting impact and truth of their profound words, which clearly demonstrate their immense power to the world.

ai.literal: Virtue called hill having climbed they who stood, anger, moment even, keeping is rare.
ai.translation: The anger of those who have climbed and stand upon the hill of virtue will rarely last even for a moment.
ai.modern: குணம் என்னும் மலையின் மீது ஏறி நின்றவர்களின் கோபம் ஒரு கணம் கூட நிலைத்து நிற்பது அரிது.
ai.explanation: The couplet describes the nature of those who have achieved great moral heights. It compares virtue to a mountain ('குன்று') that the great ones have climbed and stand upon ('ஏறி நின்றார்'). Even if such elevated people experience anger ('வெகுளி'), it is impossible ('அரிது') for it to last even for a single moment ('கணமேயும்'). The word 'காத்தல்' usually means protecting or guarding, but here it takes the sense of retaining or sustaining the anger, showing that true greatness naturally dispels negative emotions instantly.

ai.literal: The gracious ones, those who are called, are the righteous ones, indeed, towards all living beings pure compassion having taken upon oneself because of conducting.
ai.translation: Those who are called sages are the truly righteous ones, because they conduct themselves with pure compassion towards all living beings.
ai.modern: எல்லா உயிர்களிடத்தும் சிறந்த இரக்கத்தை மேற்கொண்டு நடப்பதால், அறவோர்களே அந்தணர் என்று அழைக்கப்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true nature of a sage or a gracious person. The word 'antaṇar' literally implies those possessing a beautiful, cool, and compassionate nature. The poet asserts that true sages are simply the righteous ones who extend pure compassion to every living being. Their greatness is not determined by birth or appearance, but by their unwavering kindness and ethical conduct towards all life.
